Actually is related. The appveyor is lacking vcredist. But the CI succeeds if I make the "file" step optional. I don't know what is used for, and that's why I hope that you or @graham.bloice give me an hint.

The vcredist installer ensures that the correct C runtime DLL (currently vcruntime140.dll) is installed on the system. If it's not installed, Wireshark will fail immediately at startup. I would *really* prefer to keep it mandatory. If our build servers are missing the vcredist component it's much better that the CI system complains instead shipping a surprise failure to our Windows community.

(I'd *really*, *really* prefer that Microsoft ship a less convoluted C runtime like all of the other OSes we support, but that particular windmill seems to be large and sturdy.)

Got it.

I ended up here after banging my head against the packaging on appveyor. It looks like vcredist is not installed. However, despite I forced its installation with choco (vcredist140), it isn't found. Any idea? Is it usually shipped with msbuild (in this case I should only figure out **where** it is located), or are you required to install it yourself (in this case I should install it **then** figure out where it is located).

I think the Chocolatey installer installs the vcredist package on the local machine vs downloading a deployable file. You might try switching to AppVeyor the Visual Studio 2019 image. If I found the correct setup script, it looks like it includes the Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Redist.14.Latest component:

https://github.com/appveyor/build-images/blob/master/scripts/Windows/install_vs2019.ps1

Edit: I guess it would help to read the commit. :smile: According to https://www.appveyor.com/docs/windows-images-software/, is in the list of components, so I'm not sure why this is failing.

`packaging/nsis/CMakeLists.txt` looks for vcredist_xx.exe in [several places](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/packaging/nsis/CMakeLists.txt#L71), but if you have the VC.Redist component installed it's easiest to make sure the VCINSTALLDIR environment variable is set. Our `.gitlab-ci.yml` does that by [running vcvarsall64.bat and reapplying its environment variables](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/.gitlab-ci.yml#L166).
